name: Electric-Assisted Bicycle
description: A bicycle with a seat for each rider, fully operable pedals and an electric motor of less than 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal assist to 20 mph, throttle to 20 mph, or pedal assist to 28 mph.

restrictions.rule: A seat for each rider, fully operable pedals, an electric motor of less than 750 watts, and two wheels (one at least 16 inches) or three (one at least 20 inches)
Class 1: pedal assist only, ceasing at 20 mph; Class 2: may be propelled by the motor alone, with no assistance above 20 mph; Class 3: pedal assist only, ceasing at 28 mph
The motor must disengage or stop when the rider stops pedaling or applies the brakes
A Class 3 must have a speedometer showing its speed in miles per hour
Riders of a Class 3 must be 12 or older; a younger passenger may ride on one designed to carry passengers
Every rider and passenger on a Class 3 must wear an approved bicycle helmet, on pain of a $50 fine waived on proof of buying one
Since August 1, 2020, manufacturers must permanently affix a label stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage
Must not be modified to change its class unless the manufacturer's label is replaced to match
Meets the CPSC's bicycle requirements (16 CFR part 1512)
Has the rights and duties of a bicycle and is not a motor vehicle, a motorcycle or a motorized bicycle: no driver's license or insurance
Ridden wherever bicycles are allowed, including streets, highways, bike lanes, bicycle paths and shared-use trails; may use a bike lane at a reasonable speed that doesn't endanger cyclists

A local or parish authority or state agency may ban Class 1 or Class 2 from a path or trail it manages only after notice and a public hearing, for safety or legal reasons, and may ban Class 3 outright
On a natural-surface trail designated nonmotorized, the agency that manages the trail decides whether it's allowed
